findings.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array input: `z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap and the client MultiEmail component also allows unlimited fields, enabling unbounded DB writes, email fan-out, and calendar API load within a single HTTP request
Dedupe filter in addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 is O(attendees × guests), compounding performance problems under large inputs

Every `addGuests` call emails all attendees including every previously-added guest (~O(k·A) emails for k batches ending with A attendees), each regenerating an ICS attachment, instead of only notifying affected parties
`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in email-manager.ts is O(G) per attendee
Handler passes raw `guests` (handler:167) rather than `uniqueGuests`, so the 'is new guest' branch is evaluated against unfiltered input

Server-side validation gap: server schema lacks the uniqueness `.refine` the client has, and the handler neither dedupes within `guests` nor normalizes case, so a direct tRPC call with duplicates or case variants creates duplicate Attendee rows, sends duplicate emails, and pollutes subsequent queries/ICS
Blacklist check compares a lowercased list against non-lowercased input, making it bypassable via case (e.g., `EVIL@Example.com`)

Booking query includes organizer's full credential rows (large token/key JSON payloads) via `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` but the handler never reads `booking.user.credentials` — a wasted heavy include

EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) while `evt.destinationCalendar` comes from the booking organizer, so the calendar update runs against credentials that don't own the event — likely broken/no-op calendar sync for non-organizer callers

`getTranslation` is awaited per attendee (N× translation-file load/parse per call, scaling with total attendee count and re-run on every addGuests call) instead of caching/hoisting per-locale translations

`utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx invalidates the entire bookings router (all active bookings queries across filters/tabs) instead of the specific list query, forcing full refetch of a heavy list endpoint for a one-booking change

Two team-role DB queries in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 are executed sequentially and unconditionally — before the free in-memory `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee` checks and even when `eventType.teamId` is null (running against teamId 0) — instead of short-circuiting or parallelizing

`isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses AND where the intent is OR; since a team membership holds a single role, this is effectively always false, so team admins/owners are always denied
Email failures are swallowed with a bare `console.log` (the error object isn't even logged), so the user sees 'Guests added' success regardless of whether emails were sent

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array input: `z.array(z.string().email())` in addGuests.schema.ts has no `.max()` cap and the client MultiEmail component also allows unlimited fields, enabling unbounded DB writes, email fan-out, and calendar API load within a single HTTP request

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `addGuests` mutation whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts`) defines `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/size bound. On the client, the new `MultiEmail` component allows adding an arbitrary number of email fields via repeated `updatedValue.push("")`, and `AddGuestsDialog` sends `multiEmailValue` directly to `addGuestsMutation.mutate({ bookingId, guests: multiEmailValue })`. On the server, `addGuestsHandler` performs `createMany` DB writes for all `uniqueGuests`, calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`, and then `sendAddGuestsEmails` fan-outs emails across organizers/team members and all attendees. With no cap, a single request can trigger unbounded DB writes and external side effects (email/calendar), which is a real, verifiable resource-abuse/DoS risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dedupe filter in addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 is O(attendees × guests), compounding performance problems under large inputs

adjudication.rationale: The code does compute `uniqueGuests` via `guests.filter(... booking.attendees.some(...))`, which is O(|guests|×|attendees|) (and also calls `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes`, adding another linear scan). However, the finding frames this as a “real problem” and “compounding performance problems under large inputs” without any evidence in the diff that `guests` can be large enough for this to be a clear defect; typical guest lists are small, and the dominant costs here are likely the DB update and calendar/email side effects. This is an optimization opportunity, not a verifiable bug/defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in email-manager.ts is O(G) per attendee

adjudication.rationale: In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, the code does `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` and for each attendee checks `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`. It is true that `Array.prototype.includes` is linear in `newGuests.length`, making the overall check O(A*G). However, this is a performance micro-optimization concern, not a clear defect/bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff. There’s no evidence in the diff that `attendees` or `newGuests` can be large enough for this to be a real problem, so a reasonable reviewer would treat it as a nit rather than a verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler passes raw `guests` (handler:167) rather than `uniqueGuests`, so the 'is new guest' branch is evaluated against unfiltered input

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the server filters the requested emails into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendees from `uniqueGuests`. However, it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` using the raw input array. In sendAddGuestsEmails, the conditional `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` determines which template to send to each attendee. If the caller included an email that was already an attendee, that attendee will incorrectly be treated as a “new guest” (because it’s in raw `guests`) and receive the wrong email variant. Passing `uniqueGuests` would align the email branching with who was actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking query includes organizer's full credential rows (large token/key JSON payloads) via `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` but the handler never reads `booking.user.credentials` — a wasted heavy include

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst` includes `user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true } }`. Later code only uses `booking.user?.destinationCalendar` when building `evt.destinationCalendar`, and separately fetches organizer fields via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ select: ... })`. It never reads `booking.user.credentials` (credentials are instead loaded via `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`). Therefore `credentials: true` is an unnecessary, potentially heavy include of sensitive/large credential rows, and the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is constructed from the caller's credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`) while `evt.destinationCalendar` comes from the booking organizer, so the calendar update runs against credentials that don't own the event — likely broken/no-op calendar sync for non-organizer callers

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is executed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. However, the event being updated (`evt`) is derived from the booking/organizer context (e.g., `evt.organizer` is the booking organizer, and `evt.destinationCalendar` is taken from `booking.destinationCalendar` or `booking.user.destinationCalendar`, i.e., the organizer’s configured destination). Since this mutation explicitly allows non-organizer callers (`isAttendee` and team admin/owner paths), an attendee (or other permitted non-organizer) will construct `EventManager` with *their* credentials and then attempt to update the organizer’s calendar event, which is very likely to fail/no-op (wrong account/credentials for the event owner). This mismatch is directly present in the diff and is a correctness defect for non-organizer callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getTranslation` is awaited per attendee (N× translation-file load/parse per call, scaling with total attendee count and re-run on every addGuests call) instead of caching/hoisting per-locale translations

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` is awaited inside a `.map` over `bookingAttendees.attendees` (via `attendeesListPromises`). This results in one `getTranslation` call per attendee every time `addGuestsHandler` runs, even when many attendees share the same locale, rather than reusing/hoisting a per-locale translation result. The repeated per-attendee translation fetching is directly observable in the diff; whether `getTranslation` internally caches is not shown here, but the redundant call pattern exists in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate()` in AddGuestsDialog.tsx invalidates the entire bookings router (all active bookings queries across filters/tabs) instead of the specific list query, forcing full refetch of a heavy list endpoint for a one-booking change

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the success handler calls `utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate();` with no procedure key. In tRPC React Query utils, invalidating at the router level invalidates *all* cached queries under `viewer.bookings` (e.g., list/find/get/etc.), not just the specific booking or list currently shown. That is a verifiable broad invalidation in the diff and can cause unnecessary refetches across booking views for a single-booking update (a performance defect/inefficiency).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two team-role DB queries in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 are executed sequentially and unconditionally — before the free in-memory `isOrganizer`/`isAttendee` checks and even when `eventType.teamId` is null (running against teamId 0) — instead of short-circuiting or parallelizing

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:

```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```

This performs two async role checks sequentially (second waits for first), and it runs before the cheaper in-memory checks `isOrganizer` / `isAttendee` are used in the later `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` guard. Also, when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null/undefined, it still calls both functions with `teamId ?? 0`, causing unnecessary DB queries (and potentially querying a non-existent/invalid team id). This matches the proposed finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.
